title: How To: Create a 1:1 Session
summary: Ambition's Session builder is designed to answer those questions in order, so you're never staring at a blank form wondering where to start. Here's how to create one, step by step.
body_markdown:
Coaching is the leading indicator of revenue. Almost nobody in sales leadership will argue with that. The harder question, the one CROs actually press on when they're deciding where enablement dollars go, is how anyone would know it's true. Coaching doesn't produce revenue directly; it shapes the behaviors that eventually do. A rep who gets sharper at qualifying, running discovery, and progressing deals doesn't see that show up in closed revenue for weeks. It shows up first in activities, then in the pipeline objectives those activities drive, and only later, once it's compounded, in results. Which means if you're looking for where coaching actually starts paying off, you're not going to find it in a revenue report. You're going to find it in the session itself — which makes the way that session gets built worth getting right.


That starts with a moment every coaching program runs into: the manager opens a blank scheduling screen and has to decide what this session actually is. Is it happening right now, or in two weeks? Does the rep need to prep anything beforehand? Is this a one-time conversation or the first of many? Answer those well, and the session is built with intention from the start — with a real shot at shaping the behaviors it's meant to change, instead of just filling a slot on the calendar.


**Ambition's Session builder is designed to answer those questions in order, so you're never staring at a blank form wondering where to start. Here's how to create one, step by step.**


## **1. Start a new Session**


There's no single correct door into the Session builder, and that's by design. If you're already looking at a rep's dashboard mid-week, open their Coaching tab and choose **Create Coaching → Session** . And if you just want the fastest possible path from anywhere in the platform, the Quick Actions plus-sign button takes you there in two clicks: **Quick Create → Coaching** . Use whichever entry point is closest to what you're already looking at — they all land in the same place.


## **2. Name it and give it a purpose**


Name and description are required and the objective is optional. "Amber's Weekly 1:1" tells you nothing a rep's name and a date didn't already tell you. **"Amber's Weekly 1:1 — Q3 pipeline coverage" tells you what to prep for before you've even opened the agenda.** If this session is building toward something specific — ramping a new rep, working through a slump — the objective field is where that context lives, so it's still there for you three weeks from now when you've forgotten the details.


## **3. Pick the rep, and link it to a program if one exists**


Search for the employee this session is for, and if it's part of a larger coaching Program you're already running, link it here. That one click keeps the session in the same thread as everything else you've discussed with this rep, rather than letting it float on its own as a siloed meeting nobody can trace back to the bigger picture.


## **4. Decide when and how it happens**


This is the fork in the road that shapes everything downstream. **Start Coaching Now** is the right call when you're already in the room, or already on the call, and want to run the agenda live with nothing required to save first. **Schedule Coaching For The Future** is the one most recurring 1:1s should live in — it sends a calendar invite automatically and gets the rep completing their side of the agenda before the meeting even starts, which is the single biggest lever for turning a coaching session from a status update into an actual conversation. And **Request an Update** skips the synchronous meeting altogether, useful when what you need is the rep's input, not thirty minutes on a calendar.


## **5. Set the schedule — and make it recurring**


For anything scheduled or update-based, you'll fill in the meeting date and time, along with when the agenda opens and when it's due. Using[Ambition’s calendar integration](https://ambition.com/blog/how-to-use-our-calendar-integration) makes this part a breeze. Recurrence lives in this same step: switch it on and you can set a weekly or monthly cadence, decide how far ahead of each meeting the agenda opens, and choose an end date — indefinitely, after a set number of occurrences, or on a specific date down the line.


**This is the step that turns "I keep meaning to set up a standing 1:1 with Amber" into an actual standing 1:1.** Build the recurrence once and every future session inherits the same rhythm, without you rebuilding the invite from scratch each week.


## **6. Build the agenda**


Start from a template if your team already has one — it's the faster path, and it keeps sessions consistent across managers. Building from scratch is just as easy: questions, metric snapshots, feedback prompts, polls, file uploads, even integration items that pull in a Gong or Zoom call are all available. The one rule worth remembering is that at least one agenda item has to be required in order to save — unless you chose "Start 1:1 Now" back in step 3, which skips that requirement entirely since you're running the agenda live anyway.


## **7. Add a co-coach, if this one isn't just you**


This step is optional, but worth a second look anytime someone besides you needs visibility into this session or a hand in approving it — a team lead, a peer mentor, an onboarding buddy. Adding them here means they're part of the record from the start, not looped in after the fact.


## **8. Save it**


The button in front of you changes based on what you chose back in step 3: **Create Session** for anything scheduled, **Complete Session** if you ran it live, **Request Update** if you skipped the meeting entirely. Whichever one you click, the session now lives on the rep's coaching timeline alongside everything that came before it — not as a standalone event, but as one more data point in an ongoing record.


One permissions note before you go looking for the button: creating a session requires either **Coaching: Create Session** or **Coaching: All Access** permissions. If you manage people, you can create sessions for anyone on your team by default. If you don't see the option at all, that's a permissions question for your org’s Ambition admin.


## **The takeaway**


A 1:1 Session isn't just a calendar hold with a coaching label on it — it's the container for everything that makes coaching stick: a clear purpose, a pre-built agenda, a rhythm the rep can count on. **Set it up right once, especially the recurrence, and every session after the first one is just showing up prepared.** That's the whole point of building it here instead of in a generic invite.
